2610.06584.title: Does AI Help Cyber Attackers or Defenders? Evidence from Nonpublic Vulnerabilities and Subsequent Attacks
2610.06584.paper_summary: The release decision for frontier AI systems increasingly relies on cyber capability benchmarks, yet public vulnerability benchmarks can expose agents to previously published advisories, exploits, and fixes, making it difficult to distinguish prior exposure from capability on unseen vulnerabilities. We evaluate open-weight and proprietary AI models on exploit generation, vulnerability repair and subsequent attacks in five nonpublic software environments, including vulnerabilities we privately disclosed while they remained unpatched. Researcher-developed and reviewed deterministic graders, not LLM judges, determine task scores. Comparisons with 209 disclosed vulnerabilities and cryptographic challenges reveal substantial variation across systems and vulnerability types. Repair scores exceed attack scores in two nonpublic environments and fall below them in three. Passing an initial security test is also insufficient: another exploit succeeds in 92 of 524 non-independent defender test intervals after the initial exploit is stopped. These results motivate vulnerability-specific attack-repair comparisons and subsequent resistance tests.
2610.06584.paper_summary_zh: 針對邊界 AI 系統的發布決策越來越依賴於網絡能力基準，然而公共脆弱性基準可能會使代理暴露於先前發布的建議、漏洞和修補程序，這使得難以區分先前的暴露與對未見脆弱性的能力。我們在五個非公開軟體環境中評估開放權重和專有 AI 模型在漏洞生成、脆弱性修復和隨後攻擊方面的表現，包括我們在未修補的情況下私下披露的脆弱性。由研究人員開發和審查的確定性評分器，而非 LLM 評審，來決定任務分數。與 209 個已披露的脆弱性和密碼挑戰的比較顯示出系統和脆弱性類型之間存在顯著變異。在兩個非公開環境中，修復分數超過攻擊分數，而在三個環境中則低於它們。通過初步安全測試也不足夠：在初次攻擊被阻止後，另一個漏洞在 524 個非獨立防禦者測試區間中成功了 92 次。這些結果促使了針對特定脆弱性的攻擊-修復比較和隨後的抗性測試。
